title: I made a free browser motorcycle game. How far can you get?
author: mc-rabbit
selftext:
**Game Title:** KEEP ON RIDING

**Playable Link:** [https://www.keepriding.it](https://www.keepriding.it)

**Platform**: Browser, mobile and desktop. No download, no account.

**Description:**  
KEEP ON RIDING is a [motorcycle arcade game](https://www.keepriding.it/) where the goal is to keep riding as far as you can.

You start on a tuned Piaggio Ciao. Survive one minute to unlock a Yamaha XT 600, then unlock progressively faster bikes as you go.

Along the way, you manage fuel ⛽ (smooth riding helps you save it), navigate traffic and changing road conditions, stop for fuel and supplies, and choose which route to take.

The journey starts in the Italian countryside and, if you make it, takes you all the way to the North Cape.

It’s a port of a project I started years ago, a work in progress, with new content added regularly.

\---

**Tech details:**  
[KEEP ON RIDING](https://www.keepriding.it) is a 3D browser game built with TypeScript, React, Three.js, and Web Audio, bundled with Vite/vinext. It runs as a static site with no backend, using entirely code-generated visuals and sounds.

Its \~10,500 lines of code power a deterministic 120 Hz simulation, world, weather, animals, audio, and interface, backed by \~7,200 lines of tests and automated verification tools.

\---

I'd love feedback from actual players instead of tweaking it in my own bubble.

Thanks to anyone who gives it a ride.

comments.author: Tom_Baron
comments.body:
It was pretty good fun. My 3 year old had a blast too. The controls on mobile are a bit glitchy, seemingly randomly accelerating, braking and turning semi autonomously. The information/warning banner is a bit out of place. The red one especially and is far too frequent. I dont think you need warnings for everything. You can see a cow walking across the screen.

The landing page is terrible though. Thats your first impression and funnel and yours is clearly an afterthought. Its huge in terms of impact but fortunately for you, youve done the hard work and whipping up a proper landing page shouldnt be much effort, especially with AI

replies.author: mc-rabbit
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback.  
Controls are more challenging on mobile because I chose to implement both tilt-based steering and on-screen buttons. Tilt input handling isn't consistent across different devices, particularly in terms of sensor calibration and responsiveness. I've encountered this issue in previous projects as well.

comments.author: Raqnarock
comments.body:
I kind of liked it, it has some fun parts. I noticed that you thought about details, like having animals and the game over screen. Were you inspired by the long drive and jalopy by any chance? 

As for the feedback, here are some ideas that might help you in case you want to flesh the game out more:

The main menu is a bit chaotic, I would say keep the information in the centre. Don't be afraid to get inspired by main menus from other games.

There is a lot of text on screen which is ok for the first minute but after that it would be nice to have an option where you can shut off the warnings (at the players risk). The driving has a tendency to get a bit repetitive after a while.

The random events like the animals, visitors and oil slicks, weather are a nice touch but they happen a bit too frequent. It sometimes feels like each time I want to accelerate there is either something on the road or somebody that wants to cross it. 

It would be nice if different cities, locations, types of scenery would be more spaced out. The distance scale also seems a bit too high, it does not take long for it to reach 100km, maybe you should cover less distance after a minute, 30km for example. I drove for about 3000km and in real life that would mean I could have driven from Palermo to Milano and back.

Also after getting the fourth bike, there is not a lot to do. Maybe it would be an idea for the difficulty to increase. I don't know if it is possible, but is there a possibility to split the game in different stages?

So for example the first 500km (Napoli-Rome) the weather is good and the roads are straight, the next 500km (Florence-Milano) the roads get more corners, and eventually you end up in Switzerland (Lausanne-Zürich) and the weather gets snowy and it gets very slippery, visibilty decreases and the surface will be hard to drive.

Note: I played it on PC.

replies.author: mc-rabbit
replies.body: Thanks for the very thorough feedback. I'm not familiar with The Long Drive or Jalopy, but I do travel a lot by motorcycle.

comments.author: Pleyar
comments.body: It needs a lot of polishing. Looks like a very early alpha. I appreciate the italian setting tho
